office_does: A Thurston County commissioner sits on the five-member board that is the county's legislative authority outside city limits, adopting the county budget and setting policy for services such as the sheriff and jail, land-use permitting and regional housing funding, for a four-year term.
race_blurb: One-term Commissioner Emily Clouse, a Democrat running on her housing and climate record, faces former Lacey Councilmember Nicolas Martinez-Dunning, who led the District 5 primary 38% to 35% and runs on budget integrity, deputy and jail funding and permit-fee relief. District 5 nominated the two; all county voters decide the seat.

candidates.summary: Gym owner, Marine and National Guard combat veteran and former Lacey City Councilmember (2024-2026), running on budget integrity, public safety funding, recovery-based housing and freezing permit fees.
highlights: Pledges to "protect deputy and jail funding first when budgets get tight"; endorsed by Sheriff Derek Sanders [S2]
Would back recovery-based housing with treatment and freeze the permit fees that rose January 1, 2026 [S2]
Says $20-30 million deficits are forcing cuts and that "Commissioner scandals broke public trust" [S1]
Says his campaign has rejected all PAC and special-interest money [S1]
Led the August District 5 primary with 38.36% to Clouse's 34.68% [S4]

spending.basis: Frames the race around deficits and budget integrity, pledges to report results in plain numbers and tie any fee increase to measured performance, while protecting deputy and jail funding.

housing.basis: Wants the county to welcome builders and would freeze permit fees; homelessness approach is recovery-based housing with treatment rather than a public-housing expansion.

safety.basis: Cites low deputy staffing and rising assaults and would fund deputies and the jail first; endorsed by the sheriff.

experience.basis: Challenger with about two and a half years on Lacey City Council and regional boards but no county-office record.

reform.basis: Runs on rebuilding trust after commissioner scandals, refusing PAC money and moving beyond partisan fighting.

candidates.summary: One-term District 5 commissioner, Army veteran and former DSHS forensic mental health supervisor, running on her record on affordable housing funding, climate programs and budget transparency.
highlights: As Regional Housing Council chair, oversaw approval of $25 million for affordable housing including 186 supportive units [S1]
Cites the Energize Thurston heat-pump program and $7.6 million for Deschutes Estuary restoration; pledges to implement the Comprehensive Plan's climate commitments [S1][S2]
Voted against a county budget process that cut staff and domestic-violence navigation services [S1]
Censured by the board after a 2024 investigation; the Supreme Court affirmed dismissal of a recall petition in February 2026 [S5]
Endorsed by the Thurston County Democrats, labor unions, Washington Conservation Action and Sierra Club [S2]

spending.basis: Opposed a budget that cut staff and domestic-violence services and protected animal services from cuts, alongside "fiscally responsible" and priority-based-spending language.

housing.basis: Record of approving $25 million in public affordable and supportive housing funding; pledges to expand affordable and supportive housing.

safety.basis: Cites data-driven public safety and behavioral health informed by her forensic mental health work; endorsed by gun-safety groups.

climate.basis: Record on heat-pump subsidies, estuary restoration and forest protection, chairs the Climate Mitigation Collaborative, and pledges to implement the county's climate commitments.

experience.basis: One-term incumbent running on her first-term record.
